subject: Intermittent app stalls after private cutover — packet fragmentation + NAT port exhaustion?
messages:
From: Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@sylvanhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-25T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production app stalls after private cutover

Hi Vanessa,

We cut over Sylvan's private deployment to the new VPC peering path last night and started seeing intermittent application stalls and a burst of 502/504 errors around 23:00 PDT. The issues show up when traffic scales up (load tests / morning traffic).

Attached is a short pcap and a few packet traces we captured at the edge (sylvan_edge_trace_20270725.pcap). Key observations from our side:
- Several TCP flows show retransmit storms after 1400-1500 bytes in-flight (looks like fragmentation).
- We also see TCP resets and connection reuse that lines up with client retries.
- After a high-volume period we see the app fall over until connections drain (approx 30-90s).

We suspect an MTU/fragmentation issue on the transit plus possible SNAT port churn on the Redwood NAT boxes. Can your team triage? Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Alex
Network Engineer, Sylvan Health
alex.lopez@sylvanhealth.com

--

Alex — thanks for the pcap and write-up. Looping in Marissa (PM), Karthik (Network SRE), and Mina (Infra ops) to get eyes.

Initial asks so we can prioritize:
- Which edge device saw the traces (public IP / private NHRR)?
- Can you share a short traceroute (UDP/TCP) from the Sylvan edge to the app VIP during a problem window?
- Do you have firewall logs showing drops for fragments or DF-bit events?
- Which times exactly did the burst of 502/504s occur (we want to correlate with NAT logs)?

We will start by checking NAT port allocation patterns and any recent MTU changes on our peering path. If this is MTU fragmentation being dropped midpath + NAT port churn, a two-step mitigation is likely: apply TCP MSS clamp at the peering/edge and increase NAT ephemeral port range temporarily.

I can set up a 30-min war room once we have the traceroute and timestamps.

- Vanessa Ortiz

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@sylvanhealth.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-25T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production app stalls after private cutover

Thanks for the captures — looked through the pcap quickly. Two things stand out:

1) MTU/fragmentation: I see multiple TCP segments that exceed 1500 bytes and get fragmented. Several fragments never get reassembled (we see subsequent retransmits and then resets). It looks like an intermediate hop is dropping fragments (likely a firewall or an older MPLS box that doesn't handle fragments with DF semantics).

2) NAT port churn: during the heavy load windows there is a high rate of ephemeral port allocation and reuse. A few client 5-tuple collisions line up with the app failures. If the path drops fragments that contain TCP headers (or some middleboxes rewrite headers), the NAT mapping can become inconsistent — causing half-open flows and connection failures.

Proposed short-term mitigations (apply ASAP during a maintenance window):
- Enforce TCP MSS clamp to 1350 on the Sylvan edge and our VPC peering termination so packets are never fragmented.
- Increase ephemeral port pool on the Redwood NAT cluster for Sylvan's account to reduce port reuse (temporary factor x2).
- Check stateful SG / firewall rules to ensure established/related traffic is allowed and fragments aren't being blocked.

If MSS clamp reduces fragmentation, we should see immediate improvement. We'll prepare a rollback plan in case of regressions.

I can push the MSS-clamp and NAT change, but need authorization and a short maintenance window as it will touch SNAT config.

-karthik
Network SRE, Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@sylvanhealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-25T20:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production app stalls after private cutover — proposed plan

Team,

Draft runbook we will follow if Sylvan signs off: (attached runbook_mss-clamp-rollback.md)
1) Prep: notify Sylvan support, take NAT daemon snapshot, record current ephemeral pool sizes and metrics.
2) Apply MSS clamp at edge and at VPC peering termination (1350). Monitor packet counters, retransmits, and app error rate for 15 minutes.
3) If errors persist, increase NAT ephemeral pool for Sylvan tenant by 2x and monitor for 30 minutes.
4) If successful, keep changes for 72 hours and schedule follow-up network audit (MPLS vendor + Sylvan firewall config).
5) Rollback steps documented in attached runbook.

We will need a 30-minute maintenance window during low-traffic (Sylvan suggested 02:00–02:30 PDT). Karthik and I can execute. We also will add a temporary alert for conntrack exhaustion and port reuse spikes.

Attachments: runbook_mss-clamp-rollback.md

-Mina
Infra Ops, Redwood Inference
